identity.what_it_is: A 3.5-mile Pacific-facing beach on San Francisco's west side, part of the Golden Gate National Recreation Area, known for strong currents, surf culture, and fog.
identity.where: San Francisco, California, USA — running from the Cliff House/Sutro Baths area in the north to Fort Funston in the south, paralleled by the Great Highway/Sunset Dunes corridor.
aliases: Sunset Dunes (former Great Highway segment, now a park)
identity.warnings: Scout note: 'Daly City' appearing in some geocoded data for this slug is a nearest-city artifact — the true identity is the Ocean Beach neighborhood/beach in San Francisco proper, not Daly City.

spike_candidates.statement: San Francisco closed a scenic highway to build Sunset Dunes park at Ocean Beach in 2025 — then voters recalled the supervisor who championed it.
spike_candidates.tension: Thousands showed up to enjoy the new park on opening day, but that popularity wasn't enough to save the political career of the man who fought for it.

spike_candidates.statement: San Francisco is building a $175 million seawall to save a sewage plant from Ocean Beach's shifting sand, and scientists warn it could destroy the beach itself.
spike_candidates.tension: The city still can't explain why sand vanished from the south end of the beach in the first place, yet is committing $175 million to outbuild the mystery.

spike_candidates.statement: Ocean Beach has been called California's deadliest beach, and the National Park Service deliberately chose not to install lifeguard towers there.
spike_candidates.tension: The agency's safety strategy is to let the beach look dangerous enough that people stay out of the water, rather than staff it to make swimming safer.

spike_candidates.statement: A decade after San Francisco mandated leashed dogs to protect the threatened western snowy plover, up to 70% of pet owners still ignore the rule.
spike_candidates.tension: A federal species protection exists on paper at Ocean Beach, but it depends on voluntary compliance that most dog owners simply don't give.

facts.fact: Ocean Beach is administered as part of the Golden Gate National Recreation Area by the National Park Service.
facts.quote: the beach is a part of the golden gate national recreation area, which is administered by the national park service.

facts.fact: Currents at Ocean Beach can exceed 2.5 meters per second in the inlet throat, versus about 0.5 m/s at the extreme south end of the beach.
facts.quote: currents can exceed 2.5 meters per second in the inlet throat, 1.5 meters per second at the extreme north end of the beach, and.5 meters per second at the extreme south end of the beach.

facts.fact: In 1998, a record seven people died at Ocean Beach in a single year.
facts.quote: in 1998, a record seven people lost their lives there.

facts.fact: Surfer Kirby Lee died in a surfing accident at Ocean Beach in November 2023.
facts.quote: in november 2023, surfer kirby lee died due to a surfing accident at ocean beach.

facts.fact: Jack O'Neill opened his first surf shop at Ocean Beach in 1952.
facts.quote: jack o'neill opened his first surf shop at ocean beach in 1952.

facts.fact: On November 6, 2011, Ocean Beach hosted the Rip Curl Pro, where Kelly Slater won his 11th ASP world championship at age 39 — his only title won in the continental United States.
facts.quote: on november 6, 2011, ocean beach hosted the rip curl pro surfing competition, in which kelly slater won his 11th asp world championship at the age of 39.

facts.fact: The Cliff House opened in 1863 and Sutro Baths opened in 1896, both drawing thousands of visitors to Ocean Beach.
facts.quote: the cliff house, which opened in 1863, and sutro baths, which opened in 1896, drew thousands of visitors.

facts.fact: Sutro Baths were destroyed in 1966 and the Playland amusement park was torn down in 1972, later replaced by apartment blocks and a supermarket in the 1990s.
facts.quote: after the destruction of the sutro baths in 1966, the neighborhood lost its resort appeal; the amusement park was also torn down in 1972, to be replaced by apartment blocks and a supermarket in the 1990s.

facts.fact: The clipper ship King Philip wrecked at Ocean Beach on January 25, 1878; its wreckage has resurfaced periodically since, most recently in November 2010.
facts.quote: on january 25, 1878, the king philip, a three-masted clipper ship, drifted onto ocean beach and foundered.

facts.fact: In March 2025, the Great Highway between Lincoln Boulevard and Sloat Boulevard permanently closed to traffic under Proposition K, and the resulting Sunset Dunes park officially opened April 12, 2025.
facts.quote: in march 2025, the great highway that runs along the beach became permanently closed to traffic (between lincoln boulevard and sloat boulevard), following the passing of proposition k, and 40,000 cubic yards of sand was removed from the north side of the beach to the south side of the beach.

facts.fact: 13,000 people visited the new Sunset Dunes park on its opening day.
facts.quote: 13,000 people visited the park for its opening day.

facts.fact: A skateboarding area within Sunset Dunes opened in June 2025.
facts.quote: a skateboarding area was opened in june 2025.

facts.fact: In September 2025, San Francisco district supervisor Joel Engardio was recalled from office in reaction to his support of Sunset Dunes.
facts.quote: in september 2025, joel engardio was recalled as a san francisco district supervisor, in reaction to his support of sunset dunes.

facts.fact: In January 2026, San Francisco Superior Court Judge Jeffrey Ross rejected a lawsuit that sought to undo Proposition K and reopen the Great Highway.
facts.quote: in january 2026, san francisco superior court judge jeffrey ross rejected a lawsuit that aimed to undo proposition k.

facts.fact: As of March 2026, some businesses along the former Great Highway reported sales increases since Sunset Dunes opened, while others reported only minor or negligible change.
facts.quote: some businesses along the great highway have reported increases in sales since the opening of the park, while others have reported minor or negligible changes, as of march 2026.

facts.fact: The western snowy plover, a federally threatened species, rests at Ocean Beach for 10 months of the year.
facts.quote: the western snowy plover rests at the beach for 10 months of the year.

facts.fact: Bottlenose dolphins, traditionally found in Southern California and Baja California, have migrated north to Ocean Beach's waters in recent decades as temperatures rose.
facts.quote: although they are traditionally found in southern california and the baja california peninsula in mexico, they have migrated north in recent decades, as water temperatures have risen in central california and northern california.

facts.fact: Ocean Beach is often covered with sand dollars of the species Dendraster excentricus.
facts.quote: the beach is often covered with sand dollars (specifically, the dendraster excentricus).

facts.fact: Storms during the winter of 2009-10 caused erosion that required $5 million in emergency remediation at Ocean Beach.
facts.quote: during the winter of 2009-10, storms led to $5 million for emergency remediation due to erosion.

facts.fact: The USGS predicts that 25% to 70% of the California coastline could disappear by 2100 if greenhouse gas emissions are not changed.
facts.quote: the united states geological survey predicts that 25% to 70% of the california coastline will disappear by 2100, if no changes to greenhouse gas emissions are made.

facts.fact: In 2024, the California Coastal Commission approved a $175 million plan to build one of the largest seawalls in California history along south Ocean Beach.
facts.quote: in 2024, the state's coastal commission greenlit a $175 million plan to build one of the largest seawalls in california history at the south end of the beach.
facts.source_title: The Mystery Eating Ocean Beach Alive - SF Standard

facts.fact: SFPUC's mid-2026 project update pushed the seawall's major construction start to late 2029, delayed from an earlier 2027 target, citing needed Sloat Blvd/SF Zoo intersection safety work and coordination with the California Coastal Commission.
facts.quote: the start date for major construction on the ocean beach climate change adaptation project is now anticipated for late 2029.
facts.source_title: Ocean Beach Climate Change Adaptation Project - SFPUC

facts.fact: The planned Ocean Beach seawall would span the length of nine football fields and reach 55 feet in depth.
facts.quote: the concrete barrier would span the length of nine football fields and reach 55 feet in depth to protect against nature's assault, with construction slated to start in late 2027.
facts.source_title: The Mystery Eating Ocean Beach Alive - SF Standard

facts.fact: The Oceanside Water Pollution Control Plant that the seawall is meant to protect handles more than 12 million gallons of wastewater daily.
facts.quote: the oceanside water pollution control plant handles more than 12 million gallons of wastewater each day.
facts.source_title: The Mystery Eating Ocean Beach Alive - SF Standard

facts.fact: The 2012 Ocean Beach Master Plan, a $350 million proposal to restore dunes and use a smaller buried seawall, was largely set aside when the state approved the bigger $175 million seawall in 2024.
facts.quote: the plan, which was projected to cost $350 million, recommended restoring dune ecosystems, relocating select infrastructure, and using a smaller, buried seawall to protect a vulnerable sewage overflow tunnel.
facts.source_title: The Mystery Eating Ocean Beach Alive - SF Standard

facts.fact: The city's 2021 sand replenishment at Ocean Beach cost $3.8 million, but waves swept most of the new sand away within months.
facts.quote: in 2021, the city spent $3.8 million bringing in sand from offshore sandbars.
facts.source_title: The Mystery Eating Ocean Beach Alive - SF Standard

facts.fact: As of September 13, 2026, Ocean Beach's live conditions report flagged 'life-threatening rip currents' possible in the surf zone, with a water temperature of 59°F.
facts.quote: life-threatening rip currents are possible in the surf zone.
facts.source_title: Ocean Beach Water Temp, Surf & Conditions Today - beach.report

facts.fact: Dogs must be leashed from July 1 through May 15 within the Ocean Beach snowy plover protection area, which spans stairwell 21 to Sloat Boulevard and extends 1,000 feet offshore.
facts.quote: dogs must be restrained on a leash not more than six feet in length starting july 1 and ending may 15, in ocean beach snowy plover protection area.
facts.source_title: Ocean Beach - Golden Gate National Parks Conservancy

facts.fact: A 2009-2010 Golden Gate Audubon Society survey found only about 35% compliance with the Ocean Beach leash rule; a 2019-2020 NPS survey found 70% of pets still roamed off-leash.
facts.quote: a report conducted by the golden gate audubon society between 2009 and 2010 found that compliance with dog leash requirements was approximately 35%
facts.source_title: As Snowy Plovers Return to Ocean Beach - SF Standard

facts.fact: The U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service listed the western snowy plover as a federally threatened species in 1993.
facts.quote: in 1993, the u.s. fish and wildlife service identified the western snowy plover as a federally threatened species.
facts.source_title: As Snowy Plovers Return to Ocean Beach - SF Standard

facts.fact: Beach fires at Ocean Beach are permitted only March 1 through October 31, and only in provided fire rings between stairwells 15 and 20.
facts.quote: fires are allowed only in provided fire rings between stairwells 15 and 20.
facts.source_title: Ocean Beach - Golden Gate National Parks Conservancy

facts.fact: Ocean Beach is accessible via Muni Metro at the Judah and La Playa station, and on-site parking is very limited, so the park service recommends public transportation.
facts.quote: public transportation is the best way to get to ocean beach. on-site parking is very limited.
facts.source_title: Ocean Beach - Golden Gate National Parks Conservancy

facts.fact: California's first lifesaving station was established in 1878 at the northwest corner of Golden Gate Park facing Ocean Beach and remained operational until November 1951.
facts.quote: california's first lifesaving station was established in 1878 at the northwest corner of golden gate park facing ocean beach.
facts.source_title: Vestiges of Ocean Beach - Golden Gate National Recreation Area (NPS)

facts.fact: The 'It's-It' ice cream confection was invented as a snack at Playland at the Beach, which operated at Ocean Beach from 1926 to 1972.
facts.quote: the "its-it" ice cream confection was invented as a playland snack.
facts.source_title: Vestiges of Ocean Beach - Golden Gate National Recreation Area (NPS)

facts.fact: Starting in 1895, Adolph Sutro sold oceanside lots where residents parked retired horse-drawn streetcars, forming the 'Carville' community near Ocean Beach.
facts.quote: its development began in 1895 when adolph sutro purchased several streetcars and parked them on his "oceanside" tract of land on the great highway between la playa and 48th avenues
facts.source_title: Vestiges of Ocean Beach - Golden Gate National Recreation Area (NPS)

facts.fact: Jack Johnson, the first African American world heavyweight boxing champion, trained at the Ocean Beach Pavilion in the early 1900s ahead of his famous fights.
facts.quote: jack johnson, the "galveston giant" jack johnson, the first african american world heavyweight champion, often stayed at seal rock house and trained at the ocean beach pavilion in the early 1900s.
facts.source_title: Vestiges of Ocean Beach - Golden Gate National Recreation Area (NPS)

facts.fact: The first parachute jump in America was made by Thomas Baldwin in 1887, launched from a hot air balloon departing Ocean Beach near the Cliff House.
facts.quote: the first parachute jump in america was made by thomas baldwin in 1887 - launched from a hot air balloon that departed from ocean beach near the cliff house.
facts.source_title: Vestiges of Ocean Beach - Golden Gate National Recreation Area (NPS)

facts.fact: SFGate reported Ocean Beach had claimed 8 lives since 2014, more than any other California beach, based on National Weather Service data.
facts.quote: the stingingly cold waters along the 3.5-mile stretch have claimed the lives of eight people since 2014, more than any beach in the state, according to data from the national weather service.
facts.source_title: California's Deadliest Beach Is in the Bay Area - SFGate

facts.fact: The National Park Service decided not to add lifeguard towers at Ocean Beach in order to discourage swimming there.
facts.quote: "it's not a swimming beach," said xavier agnew, supervising park ranger for the national park service. "we don't advise that anyone enter the water there."
facts.source_title: California's Deadliest Beach Is in the Bay Area - SFGate

facts.fact: On September 13, 2026, sfstation listed daily bonfire permits (6:30am-9:30pm) at Ocean Beach and a Sunset Dunes cleanup volunteer event from 1-3pm.
facts.quote: bonfires at ocean beach at ocean beach https://www.sfstation.com/ocean-beach-b264641 (6:30am - 9:30pm)

facts.fact: SFGate estimated that Ocean Beach draws more than one million visitors annually.
facts.quote: more than one million annual visitors to the city's famed ocean beach
facts.source_title: California's Deadliest Beach Is in the Bay Area - SFGate
